content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) port of the surface_wave_1d snapshot plot for FUNWAVE-TVD postprocessing (workshop version). It imports numpy/matplotlib/os (L4-L6), sets a user folder path fdir (L9), reconstructs the 1D domain m=1024, dx=1.0 (L11-L12) and bathymetry: dep initialized as an (m,m) array of 10.0 (L18), then a loop over i writes column 0 only — depth stays 10 for i < Xslp and follows 10-(x[i]-Xslp)*SLP beyond the slope start (L20-L24); DEP = dep*-1 (L26). Wavemaker rectangle around x=250 with half-width wd=10 (L29-L30), sponge rectangle x=0..180 (L31), shared y-vertices yy (L32). It creates an 8x4-inch, 600-dpi figure (L41), loads snapshot eta_00014 (L43), plots DEP[:,0] and eta[0,:] versus x plus the two overlay rectangles (L47-L49), adds grid, oblique text labels, axis [0,1024,-1,1], minor ticks and labels (L51-L61), and saves the figure to eta_1d_wave.png (L65).
entities: script (no function/class definitions; top-level Python script)
fdir — raw string, user output folder path (L9)
dep — (m,m) numpy array of depth, only column 0 modified (L18, L20-L24)

equations.expr: x = np.asarray([float(xa)*dx for xa in range(m)])

io.name: single subplot with DEP[:,0], eta[0,:], wavemaker and sponge outlines vs x

unresolved: dep is allocated as a full (m,m) matrix (L18) but only column 0 is ever computed and plotted (L20-L24, L47) — a length-m vector would suffice; whether this mirrors the MATLAB zeros(m) quirk deliberately is not stated.
Loop condition 'if i < Xslp' (L21) compares the integer index i to the coordinate Xslp=800.0; this coincides with x[i] < Xslp only because dx=1.0, so the script silently breaks for other dx.
plt.hold(True) (L51) was removed from matplotlib (deprecated 2.0, removed 3.0), so the script fails on modern matplotlib; also it is called after the plot calls it would affect.
eta is indexed as eta[0,:] (L47), i.e. the first row of a 2D array, while the MATLAB counterpart plots the whole vector; consistency with the eta_00014 file layout is not verifiable from this script.
fdir is a hardcoded user-specific path (L9); snapshot eta_00014 (L43) is hardcoded and its physical time depends on the model output interval not present here.
